pageCache.text:
Courtesy
Model the behaviours expected of others in terms of consideration, professionalism, trust and respect.
Integrity
Fair and honest, trustworthy, committed to earn success through hard-work.
Resilience
Overcome adversity to achieve success, accept consequence of mistakes and move on.
Community
A strong sense of responsibility to the community and the local environment for its residents.
Leadership
Show Leadership in thought and action, being open to new ideas and having high expectations of themselves and others.
Enthusiasm
A positive attitude towards life, passion, curiosity and a lifelong love of learning.
Welcome
Hoe Valley is a school created by a group of local parents and residents to provide high quality secondary school education to the children of south Woking.The school opened for the first time in September 2015 in temporary premises at Woking Park, and moved to our permanent home at Egley Road in September 2018. At Hoe Valley we pride ourselves on teaching a personalised curriculum which ensures students leave with excellent academic outcomes and are work ready. We are a Google School with ICT fully embedded in all curriculum areas. Preparing students for the challenges of 21st century life so they thrive safely in local, national, global and online communities.
Social Gallery
You're Invited! Join us on Wednesday 8th July for our 2026 Art Exhibition, celebrating the incredible creativity and talent of our GCSE and A-Level Art & Photography students. From striking paintings and detailed drawings to inspiring photography and mixed media, the exhibition showcases the dedication, imagination and hard work of our young artists throughout the year. Wednesday 8th July 4.15pm – 6.15pm Hoe Valley School Parents and family members are warmly invited to come along and celebrate our students' achievements. We look forward to welcoming you! #ArtExhibition #StudentArt #GCSEArt #ALevelArt #Photography
Year 11 Prom 2026 Our Year 11 students celebrated the end of their GCSE journey at their Prom, held at Pyrford Lakes Golf Club. It was a fantastic evening filled with laughter, dancing and celebrations as students came together to mark the end of an important chapter. Everyone looked amazing as they arrived in style and enjoyed a well-deserved evening with friends and staff. We are incredibly proud of everything this year group has achieved over the past five years and wish them every success as they take their next steps. Thank you for the wonderful memories, and congratulations, Year 11! #Year11 #Prom2026 #GCSEs #ClassOf2026 #SchoolProm
Year 10 Cultural Challenge at Woking College Our Year 10 students recently enjoyed an inspiring day at the Cultural Challenge at Woking College, taking part in a range of interactive workshops exploring German, French, Spanish, Chinese and the history of the USA. The day encouraged students to broaden their global awareness, discover new cultures and languages, and experience learning beyond the classroom. It was fantastic to see them embrace every opportunity with enthusiasm, curiosity and confidence. We are incredibly proud of how brilliantly they represented the school through their excellent behaviour, positive attitude and willingness to take on new challenges. Well done, Year 10! #Year10 #CulturalChallenge #LanguageLearning #GlobalCitizens #LearningBeyondTheClassroom
Our Drama students recently brought learning to life through their Theatre in Education (TIE) project! After weeks of developing and refining their performance, they welcomed Year 5 pupils from a local primary school to watch an original production exploring the importance of staying safe online. Using impressive acting, vocal and physical performance skills, our students tackled the themes of social media safety and the dangers of communicating with strangers online. Their thought-provoking performance encouraged younger pupils to think carefully about their digital choices while showcasing the creativity, confidence and professionalism of our talented performers. A fantastic achievement by everyone involved – well done! #HoeValleySchool #TheatreInEducation #DramaEducation #OnlineSafety #StaySafeOnline
A proud evening celebrating the German language! Mrs Boniface was honoured to be invited to the German Embassy for the Sommerfest der deutschen Sprache – a special event celebrating the teaching and learning of German across the UK. The German Ambassador, Susanne Baumann, thanked teachers and advocates for their dedication in opening doors to new cultures, friendships and opportunities through language learning. The evening also featured an inspiring keynote speech from former England footballer Tony Woodcock, who shared his own experiences of living and working in Germany. We are incredibly proud of Mrs Boniface and her continued passion for promoting German at Hoe Valley School. #HoeValleySchool #German #ModernForeignLanguages #LanguageLearning #GermanEmbassy
Happy Birthday, Your Majesty! Did You Know? The Monarch's Official Birthday is celebrated in June, regardless of their actual birth date. This tradition dates back more than 250 years and allows for the official celebrations to take place during the warmer summer months. From everyone at Hoe Valley School, we wish His Majesty The King a very happy Official Birthday. #KingsBirthday #OfficialBirthday #KingCharlesIII #HoeValleySchool #UnitedKingdom
Korean Club Highlights! Our Year 7 students have been getting creative while exploring Korean history, culture and traditional art. They had a fantastic time building a 3D model of Cheomseongdae, one of Korea's oldest and most famous astronomical observatories. This hands-on activity helped bring Korean history and architecture to life while encouraging creativity and teamwork. In another session, students used traditional-style ink pens to capture the delicate beauty of Korean flora, including the elegant maehwa (plum blossoms). To complete their artwork, they added personal stamps, inspired by the seals traditionally used by Korean artists throughout history. It's wonderful to see our students embracing new cultures, learning new skills and having so much fun along the way! #HoeValleySchool #KoreanClub #CulturalLearning #Year7 #CreativeLearning
International Creative Collaboration Our Year 9 Art and Photography students recently took part in an inspiring online workshop with a partner school in China. Together, they explored the traditions and symbolism of Chinese New Year before creating their own printmaking designs inspired by cultural symbols such as dragons, carp and other lucky motifs. The workshop provided a fantastic opportunity for cultural exchange, collaboration and creativity, allowing students to connect with international peers while developing their artistic skills. We are incredibly proud of the beautiful and imaginative prints they produced and the enthusiasm they showed throughout the experience. Well done to everyone involved! #HoeValleySchool #ArtAndPhotography #CulturalExchange #CreativeLearning #ChineseNewYear
Congratulations to our talented linguists! We are incredibly proud of the Hoe Valley School students who have received Official Commendations in this year's Anthea Bell Prize for Young Translators. With over 25,000 students taking part across the UK and an exceptionally high standard of entries, this is a remarkable achievement. Our students were recognised for their outstanding translation work across a range of languages, demonstrating impressive skill, dedication and attention to detail. Well done to everyone involved, your hard work has truly paid off, and we are delighted to celebrate your success. #HoeValleySchool #StudentSuccess #AntheaBellPrize #YoungTranslators #LanguagesMatter
We're hiring! As our school continues to grow, we're looking for talented, passionate and dedicated individuals to join the Hoe Valley School team. Whether you're an experienced professional or looking for your next challenge in education, we'd love to hear from you. View our current vacancies and find out more about working at Hoe Valley School: LINK IN BIO www.hoevalleyschool.org/join-us/staff-recruitment #HoeValleySchool #JoinOurTeam #NowHiring #EducationJobs #TeachingJobs
Happy World Environment Day! This week, we were delighted to welcome representatives from University College London (UCL) and the Association for Physical Education (afPE) to Hoe Valley School. As part of an exciting project exploring the links between Physical Education, sustainability and climate change education, our Year 10 students shared their ideas and perspectives on how these important topics could be combined in the future. Students took part in discussions and interviews, helping to shape resources that could support teachers and young people for years to come. A huge thank you to our Year 10 students for their thoughtful contributions and enthusiasm. It is inspiring to see young people helping to drive conversations about creating a more sustainable future. #WorldEnvironmentDay #Sustainability #ClimateEducation #PhysicalEducation #StudentVoice HoeValleySchool

Enrichment
One of the strategic aims for the School is that it should be a hub where students can explore different hobbies and interests outside of the curriculum offer. Whilst these often feed into the curriculum (for example instrumental lessons or STEM club), we also wanted to offer safe, supervised spaces after school for students to enjoy a range of clubs which may be sporting, arts based, learning a new language or developing a passion within a particular subject.
The enrichment programme is reviewed each term with input from our students and we always offer a range of clubs which are free as well as those which require a parental payment.
The enrichment programme runs from 3.30-4.30pm, Monday – Friday and ensures all students experience a broad range of exciting opportunities. Students collect house points for attendance and for excelling in a specific area, which feed into the rewards programme.

Partnerships
Train to Teach with outstanding ITT provider Xavier Teach Southeast
We always welcome people who want to discuss routes into teaching – we might be biased but we believe there is no better job than teaching young people and shaping the next generation! We would encourage anyone thinking of teaching to get in touch so that they can come to visit and find out more (SCITT Lead contact info).
We are proud to be a partner school of Xavier Teach SouthEast, a SCITT (School Centred Initial Teacher Training) provider working in and around our local area. Xavier Teach SouthEast provides all trainees with high quality training, in both primary and secondary settings, to enable them to develop into competent and confident professionals.
Trainees are well prepared through first-rate complementary placements which ensure that they gain substantial practical experience, developing their evaluative and practical teaching skills effectively. In-school expert mentors and external subject trainers have consistently high expectations and work collaboratively to ensure training is coherent and highly relevant to the needs of trainees.
Xavier Teach SouthEast have had two consecutive Outstanding judgements and are highly regarded in the local area; we love working with them and hope you will too.
For more information please call them on 01932 578 682 Or visit the website to view their prospectus or sign up to a SCITT open morning www.teachsoutheast.co.uk
If you are passionate about education and want to make an impact on the lives of our next generation, Inspiring Future Teachers – GLF Teacher Training offer a highly successful teacher training programme.
About Inspiring Future Teachers – GLF Teacher Training
Inspiring Future Teachers (IFT) is a national School Centred Provider of Initial Teacher Training (SCITT). GLF Schools’ Teacher Training is part of IFT and is an alliance of highly successful schools in Surrey and beyond. We have a very strong history of providing exceptional Initial Teacher Training since 2013, with high employment rates within our partnership schools.
Training and recruiting teachers through either our Primary or Secondary programme, allows our partnership of schools to “grow their own” and aims to offer successful candidates a long-term career pathway that goes well beyond Initial Teacher Training.
Our trainees learn in a school environment, as a member of school staff, from day one. This is supported and enhanced through a comprehensive and evidence-informed, centre-based training programme. Our train to teach programme is led by highly skilled teachers and professionals from the local area, who are passionate about education and providing the best possible life chances for the children in our schools.
Our friendly team would be happy to answer any questions that you may have about teacher training. Please contact us via email: info@glftt.org and we can arrange a call.
https://www.inspiringfutureteachers.org/glf
We work in partnership with Yes Futures to give our students a head-start in life beyond school.
Yes Futures is a multi-award winning education charity founded and run by teachers. The Yes Futures charity works with 8-18 year olds in schools across the South East. Through tailored extra-curricular personal development programmes, Yes Futures empowers young people to make ambitious choices and realise their potential. To read more about the programme please visit our Yes Futures page.

Pupil Premium and Other Funding
Pupil Premium was introduced by the Government in April 2011. From September 2012, schools now receive specific funds to support students from low-income families who are eligible for free school meals (FSM) or have been at any point in the last six years (Ever 6), looked after children (CLA) and those from families with parents in the Armed Forces (SC), under the umbrella, Pupil Premium (PP).
Schools have the autonomy to spend the funds as they wish, with the aim of reducing the attainment gap between Pupil Premium and non-Pupil Premium students. The Government and governors hold schools to account with regards to the impact of this spending and all schools are required to publish this information on their website.

pageCache.pageTitle: Hoe Valley School - Behaviour For Learning
pageCache.text:
Behaviour For Learning
Hoe Valley School has quickly built a culture of high aspiration, rigour and openness. Visitors to the School often comment on the positive atmosphere at HVS which permeates from the staff and students and on the excellent behaviour displayed. Our mantra is ‘no wasted learning time’ and as you walk around the School you can see this in all lessons. The students are incredibly proud of the School and hold one another to account.
We have appointed exceptional teachers who know every child at the School individually and we will not compromise on the quality of teaching. All of our staff, including our administrative team, are committed to ensuring that there are no ‘lost’ or ‘average’ students and that the many talents our students have are identified and nurtured.
We have a vertical house system and our students receive CIRCLE Value points which feed into individual and collective recognition and rewards. These include mufti days and trips to the cinema, bowling, laser quest and crazy golf.
Students have a Head of Year and a Tutor who are responsible for their academic progress and pastoral wellbeing. They ensure students are organised and prepared for their learning and are also the first port of call for parents who wish to contact the School.
Our approach to behaviour for learning was designed with the students and is based on the principles of choice, respect, individual responsibility and providing opportunities to ‘fix’ problems to access a fresh start. The image of a circle underpins the policy where students enter each classroom with a full circle. Poor choices cause a gap in the circle. Students are able to close the circle by addressing what went wrong, accepting the consequence and by therefore wiping the slate clean.
Anti-Bullying PolicyPDF File
Behaviour for Learning PolicyPDF File
Behaviour For Learning

Curriculum
The curriculum is the engine room of our school and before we even opened our doors the starting point was to ensure that there would never be wasted learning time. To this end, we built our curriculum around our students’ prior learning and what they need to be able to know and do in order to thrive in the future.
We considered questions such as:
The design of the curriculum was influenced heavily by the paper: ‘KS3, the wasted years’ which inspired the team to create a year 7 curriculum which is challenging, rigorous and thematically based (The Wasted Years).
As a new school, we have the luxury of creating a curriculum from scratch carefully designing and adapting its content to make it suitable for each year group, looking in detail at one year at a time. Underpinning everything though, we believe that deep, accelerated learning takes place when our curriculum meets the following 4 aims:
This means different things to different learners – for some it is studying Latin as an additional subject, for others it is perfecting the building blocks of language. However, we never want our students to repeat learning they have already consolidated but instead are always building on these foundations. Every lesson has a red, amber and green pathway contained within it and our students may follow, for example, red in Science and green in Music depending on their confidence and strengths. This is evident in lessons which are grouped by ability (Maths and Science) and those which are taught in a mixed group.
By year 9 all students are on a bespoke pathway and are accessing a range of opportunities beyond the curriculum to stretch and challenge them. These include visiting the Guardian newsroom, STEM club, studying Latin, participating in the UK Maths Challenge, industry visits to employees such as Hewlett Packard and accessing opportunities via the National Association for Able Children in Education (NACE).
The most effective learning is when students are curious, excited to know more and demonstrate a thirst for knowledge. Classrooms require energy and a ‘buzz’ as well as a clear focus on what the new learning is and what success looks like. Clear and consistent routines underpin exciting and creative classrooms.
Our learning extends far beyond the walls of the classroom, from pond dipping in Woking Park for biology to trips to museums, galleries and national newspapers, projects with global businesses and International trips.
As a Google School, all of our students access Google Classrooms for each of their subjects where they can use resources from lessons and work through independent extension activities. The Google suite of applications also enables students to work collaboratively with one another in a safe, monitored online environment.
All learning links to the ‘big question’ to clearly convey what the impact of this learning will be and how it will be useful in later life. The answer is never ‘we are learning this to pass an exam’! Instead we talk about the skills and knowledge required for different industries in 21st century life and the need for our students to be able to learn both independently and collaboratively in different contexts.
There is much in the media about the ‘UK skills gap’ and about the gap between the needs of employers and the skill set of school leavers and graduates. Through partnerships we have developed with leading local employers, we have developed the Work Ready strand to our curriculum.
This means learning at HVS enables our young people to not only have excellent academic outcomes but to confidently take up their place in the wider world. Links with universities, industry experts, different places of work and in-house ‘real world’ Work Ready skills through curriculum time. This ensures that by the time they leave the School they are well prepared for success in their chosen field.

A personalised approach is crucial to ensure that students are able to access a curriculum and broaden their knowledge and skills. Our curriculum design and delivery is data driven and all lessons offer different pathways for different students. We have a dedicated Personalisation Faculty to ensure all students are accessing an appropriate and tailored curriculum which stretches our higher attainers and supports those who find a subject or topic challenging. Home learning is completed on site during prep, allowing support for students who require it alongside a calm, well-resourced study space for more independent learners.
